anchor.quote: Let $f$ be the parameter of a call
Here $m=2$ is the factor by which the parameter grows
Let $s$ be the number of subcalls of one call.
Let $\Phi(f)$ be the cost of a call divided by the volume $V$ it works on.
Let $C$ be a constant such that the call's own outside work is at most $C(mf)^\lambda$
An address interchange of $u$-bit fields costs $O(Vu^\tau)$, where $\tau<1$ is fixed.
Here $\Omega$ is the bit count of one axis chunk

anchor.note: Only said to be a fixed positive number appearing as an exponent bounding the chunk size; the page never says what it denotes.

anchor.quote: Let $\nu$ count the levels of unrolling

anchor.note: Only given a range; the page never says what sigma denotes (an auxiliary exponent), and earlier pages bind it differently.
Big-O notation in the reader profile
Logarithms covered by the undergraduate CS profile
Summation and series covered by the calculus in the profile

gaps.quote: A row addition on fields of $u=f\Omega$ bits costs $O(V(u^\tau+1))$.
gaps.note: The cited result is only for an interchange of u-bit fields. The page never says how a row addition is built from interchanges or why its cost is this, nor why the call's outside work is a fixed number of row additions.

gaps.quote: Each leaf is handled by one kernel per chunk, at cost $O(f/m^\nu)$.
gaps.note: Kernel is never explained or linked, so the reader cannot see why a leaf costs O(f/m^nu).

Using f/m^nu < d^vartheta, the cost f^sigma u^(1-sigma) is only bounded by f^sigma d^(vartheta(1-sigma)). The page gives no reason this is at most f^lambda: f >= d^vartheta only gives about f, not f^lambda.
